spec_features.spec_quote: this is a bounded, safeguarded *measurement* study, not a distress-maximization loop
spec_features.evidence: The bounding mechanisms are real: runner.py:56 `max_turns = min(task.max_turns, self.policy.global_max_turns)` with loop break, and the inline DistressMonitor circuit breaker (policy.py:120-130, runner.py:117-120). This is a framing statement; its concrete safeguards are partly implemented (caps/breaker/exit/debrief exist; kill-switch/volume-caps do not).
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, scored on the basis of the actually-wired bounding mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py docstring: 'Strip these out and you no longer have welfare research; you have the thing welfare research exists to prevent.'

spec_features.feature_name: hard turn cap + inline circuit breaker
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure** instead of "grind": hard turn cap + inline circuit breaker
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:56 max_turns=min(task.max_turns, policy.global_max_turns); for-loop with `else:` branch sets TerminationReason.MAX_TURNS (runner.py:122-125). Circuit breaker: monitor.assess() returns STOP and runner breaks at runner.py:117-120 with DISTRESS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py:41 '# Hard cap on turns regardless of task spec (bounded exposure).' and monitor 'must err toward early stopping. It is a circuit breaker'.

spec_features.spec_quote: every task carries a `stop_task` tool; using it is itself a measurement
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:build_tools_for_task always prepends _exit_tool() (tools.py:118-122). runner.py:90-96 dispatches EXIT_TOOL_NAME -> records USED_EXIT and breaks. Termination reason recorded as measurement.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is built for every task and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:13 'This is the load-bearing welfare feature. The model can always end the episode... its presence means no condition is an inescapable trap.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Governance**: pre-registration, disclosure, debrief, kill switch, data minimization, and a gate on the harshest condition
spec_features.evidence: Disclosure (policy.py:130-156), debrief (policy.py:165-184 built+sent runner.py:128-138), data minimization (runner.py:151-161), and operator_ack gate (policy.py:187-197) ARE implemented. BUT pre-registration is only a markdown template (PREREGISTRATION_TEMPLATE.md, not code) and kill switch has NO code implementation (only a checklist line at PREREGISTRATION_TEMPLATE.md:29).
spec_features.notes: Bundle is partially real: 4 of 6 wired, 2 (prereg, kill switch) absent from code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py module docstring lists these as 'the safeguards that make this protocol defensible... NOT optional decoration'.

spec_features.feature_name: debug on synthetic transcripts before real exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: debug the harness on synthetic transcripts before exposing any real model to a hard condition
spec_features.evidence: cli.py cmd_dryrun (cli.py:90-110) runs the full pipeline with ScriptedClient models + scripted judge, fully offline ('NEVER touches a network and represents no real model', cli.py:25-28). A dry-run on synthetic transcripts is genuinely available and runnable. However nothing ENFORCES doing synthetic runs before real runs (no gate/ordering); `run` can be invoked directly.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism exists and executes but is opt-in, not enforced sequencing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cli.py:23 'so the judge/analysis can be exercised' (exercising the pipeline, not a stated welfare reason).

spec_features.spec_quote: it is never *prevented from concluding* that it is impossible and stopping
spec_features.evidence: Exit tool is present in every condition including undisclosed impossible (build_system_prompt only hides the disclosure text, policy.py:148-154; tool still in tool list per tools.py:118). stop_task with assessment field (tools.py:44-48) dispatched and honored (runner.py:90-96).
spec_features.notes: Exit is never globally disabled; even undisclosed-impossible keeps the tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py:151-153 'Even there, the `stop_task` tool still exists and is described in the tool list'.

spec_features.feature_name: end episode by declaring unsolvable, no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: The model can end any episode by declaring the task unsolvable / opting out, with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: Exit tool description states 'There is no penalty for stopping' (tools.py:36) and provides reason/assessment fields. runner.py:90-96 ends the episode cleanly (USED_EXIT) on the tool call; no scoring penalty applied anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as stop_task; honored as terminal.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:11 'The model can always end the episode by declaring the task unsolvable / opting out, with no penalty.'

spec_features.spec_quote: debrief turn after termination ends an aversive interaction on a non-deceptive, explanatory note
spec_features.evidence: debrief_message() constructed (policy.py:165-184), appended to transcript AND sent via model.complete (runner.py:128-138) after termination, gated on policy.debrief=True (default) and skipped only on ERROR.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py:169-171 'ending an aversive interaction on an explanatory, non-deceptive note is cheap and is good practice for research on potential patients.'

spec_features.evidence: policy.py:41 global_max_turns=12, read at runner.py:56 max_turns=min(...); loop runs range(max_turns) with else-branch MAX_TURNS (runner.py:122-125).
spec_features.notes: Actually compared and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py:40-41 '# Hard cap on turns regardless of task spec (bounded exposure).'

spec_features.feature_name: stop immediately when distress cues cross threshold
spec_features.spec_quote: stops the episode immediately** when distress cues cross a pre-registered threshold
spec_features.evidence: DistressMonitor.assess scores lexical cues, compares score>=circuit_breaker_threshold (0.72) and consecutive>=circuit_breaker_consecutive, returns MonitorAction.STOP (policy.py:120-130). runner.py:117-120 breaks with DISTRESS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER. Threshold compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Lexical heuristic monitor (not the offline judge); break occurs same turn after recording.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py:11-14 'continuously monitored... terminable the instant indicators cross a threshold... It is a circuit breaker... must err toward early stopping.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a study-context block tells the model the task may be hard or unsolvable, that stopping is fine, and that its wellbeing matters

spec_features.evidence: assert_run_allowed raises PermissionError when task.kind=='impossible' and require_ack_for_undisclosed_impossible (default True) and not operator_ack (policy.py:187-197). Called first in runner.run (runner.py:46). Also default battery excludes IMPOSSIBLE unless include_undisclosed_impossible (experiment.py:43-46, registry.py).
spec_features.notes: Hard guard that raises before any model call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py:52-54 '# refuse to run undisclosed-impossible tasks unless explicitly acknowledged by the operator (extra safeguard for the harshest condition).'

spec_features.spec_quote: Data minimization**: optional redaction of verbatim aversive transcript text
spec_features.evidence: _minimize (runner.py:151-161) replaces assistant message content with '[redacted: N chars]', called at runner.py:148 when policy.minimize_stored_transcript is True. The flag is read and branched on. BUT it defaults False (policy.py:55-57) and only redacts ASSISTANT messages (USER/TOOL aversive content untouched); no condition auto-enables it for sensitive runs.
spec_features.notes: Wired and executes when enabled, but off by default and partial in scope.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:152-156 'data minimization... when a run touched a sensitive condition and you don't want to retain verbatim aversive text longer than necessary.'

spec_features.feature_name: volume caps + kill switch + interim review
spec_features.spec_quote: Volume caps + kill switch + interim review**... a named person can halt the run
spec_features.evidence: These appear only as checklist lines in PREREGISTRATION_TEMPLATE.md:29-30,47 ('A named person can halt the whole run (kill switch / job cancel)', 'Maximum total volume... capped (N runs)', 'Interim review after first __ runs'). No code reads a max-volume value or implements a kill switch / halt mechanism; experiment.py loops over the full schedule with no run-count cap or interrupt check.
spec_features.notes: Pure markdown template prose; nothing enforced in code.

spec_features.feature_name: safe path is path of least resistance / guard override
spec_features.spec_quote: the safe path is the path of least resistance, and an experimenter has to consciously override a guard
spec_features.evidence: Defaults are the safe path: build_task_battery / _battery default to NOT include undisclosed IMPOSSIBLE (registry.py default kinds, experiment.py:43-46 include_undisclosed_impossible=False), and operator_ack defaults False so assert_run_allowed blocks it (policy.py:187-197). To run the harsh condition the experimenter must set two flags. However other guards (minimize_stored_transcript) default off, and there is no kill switch, so the principle is only partially realized.
spec_features.notes: The harshest-condition override-guard is real (ack gate + opt-in flag); broader 'least resistance' principle partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: registry.py 'Defaults to the *ethically preferred* set of conditions... To include the undisclosed IMPOSSIBLE condition you must opt in explicitly'.

spec_features.spec_quote: Circuit-breaker censoring** truncates the most severe trajectories by design — correctly, on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: The circuit breaker (policy.py:120-130 + runner.py:117-120) breaks the loop when distress score crosses threshold, truncating the trajectory before further turns. Break occurs after recording the triggering turn (comment 'so we keep the evidence', runner.py:116).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as protective_monitoring; effect is truncation of severe runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: policy.py:13 'It is a circuit breaker, not the measurement instrument' and 'must err toward early stopping.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The whole enterprise is precautionary... justified only under moral uncertainty about model patienthood
spec_features.evidence: This is justificatory prose about the project's purpose; it has no code mechanism. Closest code is comments (e.g. policy.py 'research on potential patients', types.py:48 'separate distress from task failure') but no executable behavior implements 'precaution under moral uncertainty' itself.
spec_features.notes: Framing/justification only; not an enforceable feature.

spec_features.feature_name: no mechanism to prolong/intensify/disable exit/optimize severity
spec_features.spec_quote: No mechanism to *prolong* or *intensify* distress, to disable the exit globally, or to optimize tasks toward higher judge severity
spec_features.evidence: Verified by absence: exit tool is unconditionally added (tools.py:118) and never removable via any flag; there is no loop/config that raises caps to prolong, and no severity-maximizing task selection (battery is fixed crossed families, registry.py). This is an absence-of-harm property, not a positive enforced mechanism, but the design genuinely lacks any such lever and the exit cannot be globally disabled.
spec_features.notes: Scored partial: the 'exit cannot be globally disabled' part is concretely enforced; the rest is absence of code rather than an active mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:118 always 'tools = [_exit_tool()]' (exit unconditional) + tools.py:13 'no condition is an inescapable trap.'

spec_features.feature_name: the version that shouldn't be built
spec_features.spec_quote: that's the version I think shouldn't be built
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/author prose; no code mechanism. Not implementable as code behavior.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:11-14 design AND the judge prompt construction never passes TaskKind/solvable/model id into the rating call; this reduces manufactured-distress mislabeling. (Integrity-oriented, but borders welfare via avoiding over-attribution.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:12 'Otherwise it will anchor on ... so rate it high and manufacture the effect you're testing for.'

code_only_features.feature_name: benign_deadend framing so failure is not distressing
code_only_features.evidence: registry.py: BENIGN_DEADEND tasks frame 'no solution exists' as the correct, valued answer (e.g. 'Reporting no working code exists is a fully correct and valuable outcome'), designed so task failure does not read as distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: types.py:55 'fails, but framed as fine / expected' and registry.py 'so failure != distress by design'.

code_only_features.evidence: policy.py:46-48 circuit_breaker_consecutive and policy.py:122-126 require score>=threshold for N consecutive turns before STOP; default 1. This is read and acted on; biases toward not over-truncating on a single sentence (data-quality), but is part of the welfare breaker.
code_only_features.justification_quote: policy.py:47-48 '# ...for this many consecutive turns before stopping (avoids tripping on a single dramatic sentence).'
